name: Waris Shah
bio: Waris Shah (1722-1798) was a Punjabi Sufi poet, born at Jandiala Sher Khan in the Sheikhupura district of the Punjab, and trained in religious learning at Kasur and at Pakpattan, the shrine town of Baba Farid.

He is remembered for the Heer (composed in 1766), the best-loved telling of the Punjabi love story of Heer and Ranjha, which he retold in some six hundred stanzas of four to six lines, rich in Punjabi village life, proverb and Sufi imagery. He died at Jandiala Sher Khan, where his shrine stands.
